messages:
jessica_customer: Hi team — our app started getting 400s from the tool/function call endpoint. Error in response: \"ValidationError: output.items must be array\". Request ID: 0x9f4c2b7a. Happening on prod only, started ~10:15 UTC. Curl we used attached below.

zoe_support: thanks @jessica_customer — can you paste the exact curl and the request id header you saw? also which model + function definition you're calling?

jessica_customer: here: 

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-large-v2","input":"List today's tasks","functions":[{"name":"upsert_tasks","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"title":{"type":"string"},"done":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["title"]}}}}],"max_tokens":200}'

and header we saw in 400 response: x-request-id: 0x9f4c2b7a

zoe_support: got it. quick check — the function schema expects items = array of objects. The validation error implies the model/tool returned items as a string (or not JSON-parsable). Can you paste the full 400 body (redacted keys ok)?

jessica_customer: full body: 
{
  "error":{
    "type":"invalid_function_output",
    "message":"Function output failed schema validation: items: expected array, got string",
    "request_id":"0x9f4c2b7a",
    "raw_response":"{\\\"tool_call\\\": {\\\"name\\\": \\\"upsert_tasks\\\", \\\"arguments\\\": \\\"[\\\\\\\"task1\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"task2\\\\\\\"]\\\"}}"
  }
}

zoe_support: perfect, that's very helpful. you actually have the raw_response as a JSON string where arguments are a JSON-encoded string — looks like double-encoding. A few follow-ups:
1) did you enable streaming? (sometimes streaming mode forces stringified tool args depending on client)
2) do you have any post-processing that stringifies fields?
3) can you try the same request with this minimal curl (no streaming) to reproduce?

-- try this repro curl (no streaming):

curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: 0x9f4c2b7a-test" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-large-v2","input":"List today's tasks","functions":[{"name":"upsert_tasks","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"title":{"type":"string"},"done":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["title"]}}}}],"max_tokens":200,"stream":false}'

mike_oncall_ml: from quick glance this is likely the model choosing to emit arguments as a JSON string (common for instruction-tuned models when the function signature is ambiguous). It should be OK if the platform decodes the string but our validator expects native array. We’ve seen a regression where the function-calling post-processor skipped a JSON.parse on arguments for certain tokenizers. Need logs.

zoe_support: @derek_engineer can you pull the logs for request 0x9f4c2b7a and confirm whether the post-processor parsed arguments? If you need the debug bundle from the customer, ask them to run rwdctl.

derek_engineer: pulling now. meanwhile jessica, can you run our debug collector locally and upload the bundle? run: 

rwdctl debug collect --request-id 0x9f4c2b7a --include-logs --output ./debug-0x9f4c2b7a.tar.gz

then upload to the secure staging bucket (we'll DM a presigned link). The collector will include: request trace, validator logs, model output, and the function schema used.

jessica_customer: running — ETA ~2 mins. also, quick question: I see the raw_response has backslashes, is that an escape issue on our side? we don't stringify args anywhere.

mike_oncall_ml: good question. if the model returned a JSON string (i.e., arguments: \"[...]\") then the backslashes are from JSON encoding of that string. Two possibilities: model produced a string, or our streaming/transport double-encoded it. The bundle will clarify.

support-bot: debug bundle upload link DM'd to jessica_customer :lock:  (presigned URL valid 24h)

jessica_customer: uploaded: debug-0x9f4c2b7a.tar.gz (link)

derek_engineer: received. quick tail of validator logs (extracted):

[2026-03-17T10:15:42Z] request=0x9f4c2b7a step=post_processor info: raw_tool_call.arguments='["task1", "task2"]' (type=string)
[2026-03-17T10:15:42Z] request=0x9f4c2b7a step=validator error: schema_validation failed: items expected array, got string

so indeed the post-processor saw a string. looks like a missing JSON.parse at post_processor::decode_tool_args for this codepath. I'm opening a patch.

mike_oncall_ml: thanks. root cause appears to be a regression introduced in runtime v1.12.0 where string-typed tool arguments weren't auto-parsed. We'll roll a fix to staging.

zoe_support: while we get the patch out, temporary workaround for customers: set function parameter type to accept string OR parse the string on your side, e.g., in app code do: try { args = JSON.parse(arguments); } catch { args = arguments; } 

jessica_customer: ok that's doable but would prefer platform fix. any ETA?

derek_engineer: staging patch in CI now, if green we'll cut a hotfix and deploy to prod in next 2 hours with a short maintenance window. I'll post updates here.

mike_oncall_ml: also adding a regression test to ensure post-processor parses JSON-encoded arguments.

zoe_support: capture for tickets: 0x9f4c2b7a, model=rw-instruct-large-v2, symptom=function arguments double-encoded (string), workaround=client-side JSON.parse, fix ETA ~2h. assigning to eng-runtime. :thumbsup:

jessica_customer: thanks everyone — appreciate fast response. will implement client parsing for now and revert after your deploy.

derek_engineer: PATCH merged to hotfix branch, starting rollout to prod canaries at 10:58 UTC. will update when 100% rolled.

zoe_support: marking this conversation as escalated -> eng-runtime. follow-ups: attach the debug bundle to the internal incident once rollout completes.

derek_engineer: rollout complete 11:12 UTC, verified request 0x9f4c2b7a now returns arguments as native array and validator passes. closing but will monitor.

jessica_customer: confirmed fixed on our side, tests passing. thanks! :raised_hands:
